csv_project_name: DB for Pool Conversion Into Fitness Center
csv_scope_of_work: Allegany College of Maryland is seeking proposals from qualified contractor/design teams to complete a design/build project to convert our approximately 6,180 square foot indoor, in-ground pool and surrounding space in our Physical Education Building into a new fitness center. As part of this project, the winning bidder will provide all drawings, specifications, and construction services for the project. This will be a turn-key project, in which the winning bidder will take the project from design through the completion of construction. Project will consist of engineering, design, and construction that will transform the current pool area into a spacious new fitness center for students, faculty, staff, and the community to enjoy as a year-round health and wellness space
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Design Build/Developer, Programming, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering

title: Design-Build for Pool Conversion into Fitness Center
short_description: Design-build conversion of an indoor pool area into a new college fitness center.
project_scope: Conversion of an approximately 6,180 square foot indoor in-ground pool and surrounding space within the Physical Education Building at Allegany College of Maryland into a new year-round fitness center. The project includes transformation of the existing pool area into a fitness space for students, faculty, staff, and the community.
services: Turnkey design-build services including engineering, design, drawings, specifications, and construction services; requested disciplines include architecture, programming, civil engineering, electrical engineering, and mechanical engineering.
relevance_explanation:
- Small interior building conversion project with limited structural ambition.
- Primarily a fitness center fit-out/adaptive reuse, not a bridge, long-span roof, stadium, or special structure.
- Includes design-build and engineering scope, but likely dominated by architectural/MEP renovation work.
- Construction budget is relatively low, reducing strategic relevance for sbp.
